title: Digital Technology and Culture - Web Design and Development Option (Pullman only)
sourceText:
DTC 101 [ARTS]

ENGLISH 101 [WRTG]

Quantitative Reasoning [QUAN]

Foreign Language, if needed, or Electives
Electives or DTC Electives must include an additional [M] course to meet the University requirements of two [M] courses.
Electives must include sufficient 300-400-level coursework to meet the University requirement of 40 credits of upper-division coursework. May need to include a writing in the major [M] course to meet University requirements.
Two years of high school foreign language or at least two semesters of college-level foreign language are required by the College of Arts and Sciences for graduation.

DTC 201

DTC 202 [COMM]

HISTORY 105 [ROOT]

Biological Sciences [BSCI] with lab
To meet College of Arts and Sciences requirements, students must complete 1 additional lab credit of [BSCI] or [PSCI] for a total of 8 credits (2 labs).

DTC 206 [EQJS] or 475 [DIVR]

Humanities [HUM]

Electives
Electives or DTC Electives must include an additional [M] course to meet the University requirements of two [M] courses.
Electives must include sufficient 300-400-level coursework to meet the University requirement of 40 credits of upper-division coursework. May need to include a writing in the major [M] course to meet University requirements.

DTC 330 or 331

Physical Sciences [PSCI] with lab
To meet College of Arts and Sciences requirements, students must complete 1 additional lab credit of [BSCI] or [PSCI] for a total of 8 credits (2 labs).

Social Sciences [SSCI]

Complete Writing Portfolio

DTC 301 [M]

DTC 355

Equity and Justice [EQJS] or Diversity [DIVR]
Depending on whether a student takes DTC 206 [EQJS] or DTC 475 [DIVR] for their degree requirement, they should take a UCORE option that fulfills the opposite requirement in their third year.

DTC 477

DTC Electives
Electives or DTC Electives must include an additional [M] course to meet the University requirements of two [M] courses.
DTC Electives (12 credits): Any DTC course not included in the degree requirements is eligible to be a DTC elective. One DTC elective course (3 credits) may be substituted by DTC 498 or 499.

DTC 497 [CAPS]

DTC 498 or 478
Students who elect to take DTC 478 need to have taken DTC 355 as a prerequisite.

Senior Exit Survey

This option explores the principles of web design, web coding, user experience (UX), content management, information architecture, usability, accessibility, and more. Students in this option will learn HTML, CSS, and scripting languages such as JavaScript or PHP. Graduates of this track will be able to create and manage websites through all stages of development, from planning and setup, to developing and managing code and content.

This option is available on the Pullman campus. A student may be admitted to the DTC – Web Development Option upon making their intention known to the department. This option requires 42 credits of major-specific coursework.
